Hi Katie —

Good questions — thanks for sending the volume sheet. Below is a concise breakdown and three concrete examples (numbers rounded for clarity). I also include the commercial note at the bottom. If any part of the model family matters for you, tell me which model you plan to run and I’ll map the pricing exactly.

High level:
- Input tokens = everything sent to the model at request time. That includes the system message(s), user messages, assistant messages used as context, plus any tool/function call arguments that are provided as part of the request body.
- Output tokens = tokens generated by the model in the response (what comes back in the "assistant" message or streamed token frames).
- Tool tokens: when Redwood executes a tool call that includes additional text payloads (e.g., you pass a long JSON to a retrieval tool), those tokens are counted as input tokens in the request that contains them. If a tool result is later passed back into the model as part of a new request, those tokens are counted again in that new request's input.
- Rounding / billing granularity: we bill at per-token granularity (no 100-token buckets). Each request is computed as: billed_input_tokens = ceil(actual_input_tokens), billed_output_tokens = ceil(actual_output_tokens). We do not aggregate/round across requests; we sum ceil(input)+ceil(output) across requests in the billing cycle. For streaming partial responses, we bill tokens as they are generated — same ceil per request snapshot.

Examples (concrete):
1) Simple chat (system + user prompt):
   - system message: 12 tokens
   - user prompt: 46 tokens
   - model reply: 78 tokens
   Calculation: input = 12 + 46 = 58 -> billed_input = ceil(58) = 58
                output = 78 -> billed_output = ceil(78) = 78
                total billed tokens for request = 58 + 78 = 136

2) Tool call with arguments included in request body:
   - system: 8 tokens
   - user prompt: 32 tokens
   - tool args (search query + filters): 22 tokens
   - model performs a function call; we serialize the tool args and include them in the request — they are part of input. Model returns a function call object (10 tokens) and the server executes the tool, returns a 140-token JSON result which we include in a follow-up request context to the model.
   Step A (initial request): input = 8+32+22 = 62 -> billed_input_A = 62; output_A = 10 -> billed_output_A = 10; total_A = 72
   Step B (follow-up request with tool output in context): input_B = 8 (system) + 32 (user) + 140 (tool result) = 180 -> billed_input_B = 180; model final reply = 95 -> billed_output_B = 95; total_B = 275
   Combined billed tokens across the two requests = 72 + 275 = 347
   Note: tool payloads are not exempt — if you pass large retrieval results into the model, those tokens will be billed as input each time they are included.

3) Short, high-frequency calls (edge-case for rounding):
   - system: 4 tokens
   - user: 6 tokens
   - model reply: 5 tokens
   For one such request: billed_input = ceil(10) = 10, billed_output = ceil(5) = 5, total = 15. If you make 10,000 of these tiny calls, total billed tokens = 150k (no extra hidden rounding across requests). That is why high-QPS tiny calls can be inefficient: every request still carries system/user context tokens.

Model family notes: smaller context/encoding differences can slightly change token counts; for the same raw text, different tokenizers may differ by a token or two. We test and publish per-model tokenization deltas on the catalog page; for pricing comparisons we recommend running a short sample (we can help) to get exact deltas.

Commercial note (commit/discount):
- Baseline hosted list rate: model-dependent per-token rates (I can map to the exact model you plan to use).
- For a $50k/month committed hosted contract we typically provide a 15-25% discount on list token rates (range depends on model mix and term length).
- Proposal: 20% off list for a 12-month commit at $50k/mo; includes a one-time red flag review and 30 days of premium support.

I’ll attach a short worked example using your volume sheet and map it to list vs committed pricing if you want — want me to run that and share the workbook?

—Rachel

Ben/Rachel — quick confirmation from pricing operations: billing math we use is: for each API request we compute the final token counts observed for input and output during that request lifecycle. For streaming responses we tally tokens as they are emitted but the final billed_output for that request is ceil(total_emitted_tokens_for_request). There is no intermediate snapshot rounding that would double-count within a single request. In short: per-request ceil on final input and final output counts; we then sum across requests for the invoice.

Also, for negotiated tiers we can offer per-request minimums if the customer prefers (for example, a negotiated effective floor of 10 tokens per request) — but that is a commercial concession and reduces variability for both parties. We can add that to the term sheet if helpful.

Marissa

Katie — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps:

1) Streaming tool results & summaries: yes — if you can reduce the tokens you pass into the model (e.g., send a 25-token summary instead of the full 1,200-token retrieval), you reduce billed input tokens proportionally. We can help design a concise summary stage on our side (we've built small summarizers that run pre-model to trim retrievals).

2) Blended / per-request floor: we can do a blended approach. Example term options we'll put in the draft:
   - Option A (simple commit): $50k/mo, 12 months, 20% off list token rates, standard per-token billing as described.
   - Option B (blended for high-QPS tiny calls): $45k/mo, 12 months, 18% off list; plus a negotiated per-request floor of 8 tokens for calls under 20 tokens (so any request with total < 8 would be billed as 8). This reduces volatility on both sides and is useful for very chatty tooling patterns.

I've asked Marissa to produce the worked example against your sheet and to include projected monthly invoices under Options A/B. We'll attach a redlineable term sheet and a sample invoice. Ben — can you approve the pricing buckets (20% / 18%) for the deal desk so we can send out LOI language?

Next steps: Marissa will share the workbook Monday, I'll send the term sheet and a short implementation note on the summarizer approach.

Thanks —
Rachel
